title: Detect, analyze, prevent deadlocks — jstack, findDeadlockedThreads, tryLock, ReadWriteLock
shortTitle: How do you detect and prevent deadlocks?

s1_definition.profdef: **Detection**: `jstack <PID>` dumps all thread states — JVM automatically detects deadlocks and prints "Found one Java-level deadlock" with the threads and locks involved. Programmatically: `ThreadMXBean.findDeadlockedThreads()` returns IDs of deadlocked threads. **Analysis**: read the thread dump — identify which threads hold which locks and which locks they're waiting for. The circular dependency is the deadlock. **Prevention**: (1) **Lock ordering** — always acquire multiple locks in a deterministic order (by ID, hash). (2) **tryLock with timeout** — `ReentrantLock.tryLock(5, SECONDS)` backs off instead of waiting forever. (3) **ReadWriteLock** — multiple readers concurrently, writers exclusive — reduces lock contention. (4) **Avoid nested locks** — redesign to use a single lock or lock-free structures. (5) **Lock-free** — AtomicInteger, ConcurrentHashMap — no locks at all.
s1_definition.analogy: **Detection**: the bank manager does a ROLL CALL (jstack) — "Who is standing where, holding what key, waiting for what?" Finds: "Teller-1 in Vault-A, waiting for Vault-B key. Teller-2 in Vault-B, waiting for Vault-A key." DEADLOCK found! **Prevention**: (1) Rule: always enter lower-numbered vault first. (2) Try the key for 5 minutes — if it doesn't work, step back and retry later (tryLock). (3) For reading: multiple tellers can read the register simultaneously — only lock for writing (ReadWriteLock).
s1_definition.oneliner: Detect: jstack + findDeadlockedThreads(). Prevent: lock ordering (break circular wait), tryLock(timeout) (break hold-and-wait), ReadWriteLock (reduce contention), lock-free structures (eliminate locks).

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The trade settlement service deadlocked during peak hours.** 200 settlement threads, some transferring A→B, others B→A → deadlock. Detection: ops team ran `jstack` → found "Java-level deadlock." Analysis: Thread-47 held lock on ACC-001, waiting for ACC-002. Thread-112 held ACC-002, waiting for ACC-001. Fix: (1) Immediate: restart service. (2) Long-term: lock ordering by account ID. (3) Added deadlock monitoring: scheduled task calling `findDeadlockedThreads()` every 30 seconds → PagerDuty alert. (4) Replaced balance reads with ReadWriteLock → 10x more concurrent reads.
sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (Detection).** Ops team notices settlement service is stuck. Runs `jstack <PID>`. Output shows: "Found one Java-level deadlock" — Thread-47 holds ACC-001 lock, waits for ACC-002. Thread-112 holds ACC-002, waits for ACC-001.

**Step 2 (Immediate fix).** Restart service. All pending settlements re-queued from Kafka.

**Step 3 (Long-term fix).** Implement lock ordering by account ID. Add deadlock monitoring: scheduled task every 30s calls `findDeadlockedThreads()` → PagerDuty alert.

**Step 4 (Optimization).** Replace synchronized balance reads with ReadWriteLock. 100 balance inquiries/sec → ALL concurrent with readLock. Only debits/credits take writeLock (exclusive). 10x throughput improvement for reads.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ DEADLOCK DETECTION + PREVENTION TOOLKIT ═══

  DETECT:
  ├─ jstack <PID>                  → thread dump, auto-detects deadlock
  ├─ ThreadMXBean.findDeadlockedThreads() → programmatic, schedule every 30s
  ├─ VisualVM / JConsole           → GUI, live thread monitoring
  └─ Thread dump on SIGQUIT        → kill -3 <PID> on Linux

  PREVENT:
  ├─ Lock ordering (by ID)         → break circular wait
  ├─ tryLock(timeout)              → back off if can't acquire
  ├─ ReadWriteLock                 → multiple readers, reduce contention
  ├─ Single lock                   → no nested locks (but less concurrency)
  └─ Lock-free (Atomic/CHM)       → eliminate locks entirely

  ═══ ReadWriteLock ═══
  readLock:  [Reader1][Reader2][Reader3] → ALL concurrent! (Recommended) 
  writeLock: [Writer1] → EXCLUSIVE, blocks all readers and writers
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Deadlock Prevention Classes ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  <<interface>> ReadWriteLock          │
  │  + readLock(): Lock                  │  multiple readers concurrent
  │  + writeLock(): Lock                 │  exclusive writer
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                  │ implements
  ┌───────────────▼──────────────────────┐
  │  ReentrantReadWriteLock              │
  │  - readerCount: int                  │
  │  - writerThread: Thread              │
  │  + readLock(): Lock (shared)         │
  │  + writeLock(): Lock (exclusive)     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ReentrantLock                       │
  │  + lock(): void                      │  blocks forever
  │  + tryLock(timeout, unit): boolean   │  backs off on timeout!
  │  + lockInterruptibly(): void         │  can be interrupted
  │  + unlock(): void                    │  MUST be in finally!
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  DeadlockMonitor (scheduled task)    │
  │  - tmx: ThreadMXBean                 │
  │  - alertService: PagerDutyClient     │
  │  + check(): void                     │
  │    deadlocked = tmx.findDeadlockedThreads()│
  │    if (deadlocked != null)           │
  │      alertService.fire("DEADLOCK!")  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Deadlock detection: `jstack <PID>` prints thread dumps and automatically identifies deadlocks with "Found one Java-level deadlock." Programmatically: `ThreadMXBean.findDeadlockedThreads()` — schedule this every 30 seconds as a health check, alert via PagerDuty if non-null. Prevention strategies in order of preference: (1) Lock ordering — always acquire in deterministic order (by account ID) → breaks circular wait. (2) `tryLock(timeout)` — gives up after timeout instead of waiting forever → breaks hold-and-wait. (3) ReadWriteLock — multiple readers concurrently (readLock is shared), only writers exclusive → reduces contention that leads to deadlock. (4) Lock-free structures — AtomicInteger, ConcurrentHashMap — no locks at all.

ReadWriteLock is especially valuable in banking: 95% of balance operations are READS (balance inquiry, statement view). With synchronized: all reads serialized. With ReadWriteLock: all reads concurrent, only writes exclusive. 10x throughput improvement. In production: combine lock ordering (code level), tryLock (fallback), ReadWriteLock (read-heavy optimization), and deadlock monitoring (alerting) — defense in depth.
